## 1. Identity

| | |
|---|---|
| Task | T-025 |
| Title | Writers for the base tables a ruled task must write |
| Wave | 3 |
| Layer (CLAUDE.md §3) | 2 |
| Kind | **TOOLING** (CLAUDE.md rule 10: tooling and research never share a pull request) |
| Executor | Sonnet-class |
| Traces to | IMP-19 in `scratchpad/session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit/audit/hs-improvement-programme.md` |

## 2. Preconditions

- **The integration base.** This workplan must be on the branch you start from. If the workplan's pull request is merged, that is `origin/main`. Until then it is the workplan branch, `origin/ccr-408aaa9b-z3e4s0` (if that name is gone: `git branch -r --contains "$(git log --all --format=%H -1 -- workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN.md)"`). Every command in this file uses `$BASE`, set by the first line of the set-up block, and never a literal `origin/main`: on a base that lacks the workplan, a diff against `origin/main` contains the whole workplan and every gate and co
- **Tasks that must be merged to the integration base first:** T-024 merged. Check by running that task's own after-test (its section 6), or `git log "$BASE" --oneline | grep -F "<that task's commit subject>"`.
- **What this task takes from T-024** (added 2026-11-13 from the pilot). `add-lang-jur-pair` (section 4) refuses a jurisdiction through `dbcore.check_jurisdiction`, which after T-024 reads the table `base_jurisdictions`; and the approval pointer of section 4 is the one `add-jurisdiction` takes (`--approval-ref`, a dated `## ` heading of the ledger found exactly once). Confirm both on `$BASE` before you start: `git grep -n -e 'def declared_jurisdictions' -e 'def check_jurisdiction' -- scripts/dbcore.py` prints both, and `git grep -n -A2 'sub.add_parser("add-jurisdiction"' -- scripts/db.py; git 
- **Owner decisions:** none. This task rests on rulings already in the ledger or on no ruling at all.
- **Tests that must be red (or green) before you start:** AT-104 red. (`AT-` numbers are the acceptance tests of `scratchpad/session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit/audit/hs-improvement-programme.md` §4, §7 and §9 and of `scratchpad/session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit/audit/td-requirements-and-interface-spec.md`; the test this task must turn is restated in full in section 6, so you do not need to open either.)
- **Set-up.**
- **Pilot or dry run** (a scratch clone, no pull request): do not run `/session-open`, do not touch `scratchpad/CURRENT`, stay on the branch you were given instead of `git switch -c`, and stop after section 7 (no push, no pull request, no `/batch-done`). Say in your report that it was a pilot.

## 3. The problem, in the guidebook's terms

The language–jurisdiction pairs and the identity registry can be changed only by hand-written SQL, which bypasses every refusal; they are also outside the captured set, so a change would not reach a migration.

**Evidence command** (run from the repository root, after the set-up block so that `$SCRATCH` exists; it reads the canonical database read-only or works on a copy):

```
python3 -I -c "import sys,sqlite3;sys.path.insert(0,'scripts');import dbcore;c=sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro',uri=True);print(sorted({r[0] for r in c.execute(\"select name from sqlite_master where type='table'\")}-set(dbcore.writable_tables(c))))"
```

**Expected output today:** The list includes `lang_jur_map` and `base_taxonomy_identity`. It also prints other tables (read 2026-11-13: twelve more, among them `data_migrations` and `sqlite_sequence`, which `dbcore.NOT_CAPTURED` excludes by design); they are not this task's. Save the output (`> "$SCRATCH/evidence-before.txt"`). **After the change** the same command must print the same list with exactly those two names removed: the command prints one line, so `diff "$SCRATCH/evidence-before.txt" "$SCRATCH/evidence-after.txt"` shows that line changed, and the only names missing from the new line are those two.

If the output differs, the ground has moved: stop (section 9). Ids that appear in this command are probes read on 2026-11-12; where the command derives an id by query, that is deliberate, and a test you write must do the same (section 6).

## 4. The change

Order of preference, from CLAUDE.md §8: do nothing and say why; change a rule or convention; reuse what exists; delete the cause; only then add the smallest code that closes the defect.

1. **Four verbs in `scripts/db.py`, two per table,** each with the refusals that are its value. (This item said "two verbs only" and then listed four operations; the pilot built four, and the readers need all four.) The history of the requirement: an identity code added with an optional `--parent` (the existing `parent_code` column; T-102 needs it: the device decomposition of the owner's OD-14 answer makes `MOB` a parent) and an amend of its display name with the replaced value printed; [added 2026-11-12, OI-13 fold] the amend also takes `--description` and `--category`, because the names and descriptions of `LLD` and `UPL` are proposals the owner confirms after they are written (T-102, T-116), so correcting one must be one verb call, not a migration by hand. Add no history or provenance column (no reader yet: `T-102-design.md` section 12, H).
   - **Chosen (pilot 2026-11-13, corrected at the fold): one approval pointer for all four verbs, `--approval-ref`,** the full text of a dated `## ` heading of `references/project-standards.md` found exactly once (`dbcore.ledger_heading_count`; a leading `## ` is stripped). Reason: it is the shape `db.py` already uses for an owner's approval of a base-vocabulary entry (`mint-term-from-catalogue --approval-ref`, re-read by `validate_parameters` P2) and the one T-024's `add-jurisdiction` takes for the same kind of act (admitting a base code), so one family of base admissions has one pointer. raise Refusal(
                f"add-alias: --seed {seed} is withheld (OR-17: the model may not generate its "
                f"own phrases, names or aliases). Whether a model-made search aid may be "
                f"written at all is an open owner question; the column and the existing rows "
                f"keep the value. An owner-supplied seed takes --seed owner_supplied "
                f"--approval-ref. Nothing was written.")
        if approval_ref is None or not approval_ref.strip():
            raise Refusal("add-alias: --seed owner_supplied needs --approval-ref, the dated `## ` "
                          "heading of the ledger entry that records the owner supplying this "
                          "alias; an owner-supplied seed with no recorded owner statement is "
                          "a model's. Nothing was written.")
        approval_ref = approval_ref.strip()
        if not re.search(r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}", approval_ref):
            raise Refusal(f"add-alias: --approval-ref {approval_ref!r} carries no date. Give the "
                          f"dated `## ` heading of the approving ledger entry.")
        n = dbcore.ledger_heading_count(approval_ref)
        if n != 1:
            raise Refusal(f"add-alias: --approval-ref {approval_ref!r} is the heading of {n} "
                          f"ledger entries; it must be exactly one. Nothing was written.")
        if approval_ref.startswith(dbcore.LEDGER_DELEGATED_PREFIX):
            raise Refusal(f"add-alias: --approval-ref {approval_ref!r} is a delegated resolution "
                          f"(a model's), not the owner's words. Nothing was written.")
        if not dbcore.ledger_entry_names(approval_ref, alias.strip()):
            raise Refusal(f"add-alias: the ledger entry {approval_ref!r} does not name "
                          f"{alias.strip()!r}. Record the owner supplying this alias in a dated "
                          f"entry that names it, then give that entry's heading.")
    elif approval_ref is not None:
        raise Refusal("add-alias: --approval-ref belongs to --seed owner_supplied. Nothing was written.")
    if attestation is not None and route != "seed" and attestation not in dbcore.ATTESTED_FORMS:
        raise Refusal(f"add-alias: --attestation {attestation!r}: a form read in a source is "
                      f"instrument (a code, standard or statute uses it) or other_source. A seed "
                      f"takes --seed. Nothing was written.")
    if route == "base":
        missing = [f for f, v in (("--language", language), ("--jurisdiction", jurisdiction),
                                  ("--source-url", source_url), ("--attestation", attestation))

        original_title              TEXT,
        edition                     TEXT,
    , verified_by_tool TEXT, last_verified_at TEXT, verification_attempt_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0, superseded_by_ref_id TEXT, pages TEXT, pub_month INTEGER, language TEXT, subtype TEXT, citation_count 
CREATE VIEW v_evidence_authors AS
SELECT
  e.ref_id                                                                   AS ref_id,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM evidence_source_authors a
     WHERE a.ref_id = e.ref_id)                                              AS author_count,
  (SELECT CASE WHEN a.is_corporate = 1 THEN a.corporate_name ELSE a.last_name END
     FROM evidence_source_authors a
     WHERE a.ref_id = e.ref_id ORDER BY a.position LIMIT 1)                  AS first_author_last,
  (SELECT CASE WHEN a.is_corporate = 1 THEN NULL ELSE a.first_name END
     FROM evidence_source_authors a
     WHERE a.ref_id = e.ref_id ORDER BY a.position LIMIT 1)                  AS first_author_first,
  (SELECT CASE WHEN a.is_corporate = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
     FROM evidence_source_authors a
     WHERE a.ref_id = e.ref_id ORDER BY a.position LIMIT 1)                  AS is_corporate_primary,
  (SELECT group_concat(
            CASE WHEN a.is_corporate = 1 THEN COALESCE(a.corporate_name, '')
                 ELSE TRIM(COALESCE(a.last_name, '') || ' ' ||
                           substr(COALESCE(a.first_name, ''), 1, 1)) END,
            '; ' ORDER BY a.position)
     FROM evidence_source_authors a
     WHERE a.ref_id = e.ref_id)                                              AS author_display
FROM evidence_sources e

When a BPC cites a T4–T6 source, the citation must additionally confirm that the cited edition is the **current legally-in-force edition** — not a superseded edition. Pre-existing supersession_check rows surface this for the supersession protocol; the same check applies inline to any new T4–T6 citation.

**Enforcement.** The currency fact is carried in the `evidence_sources.code_currency_*` columns; no mechanical check reads it since `scripts/audit/code_currency_audit.py` was deleted (plan step 1.6, RULINGS R4).

`code_currency_status` enum: `VERIFIED-CURRENT`, `PERMANENT-FRAMEWORK` (foundational references like CRPD, ICF, WHO Child Growth Standards that do not revise on the same cadence), `SUPERSEDED-PENDING-REPLACEMENT`, `UNVERIFIED-CHECK-DEFERRED` (e.g., T6 codes flagged in MOB Pass-2 supersession audit as out-of-scope per DR-2026-05-24).

Worked example surfaced 2026-05-25: `accessible-circulation-geometry.md` cites DIN 18040-1:2010-10. The 2010 edition is still legally in force in Germany (referenced in MVV TB 2024/1 published August 2024), but draft revision E DIN 18040-1:2023-02 exists and DIN EN 17210:2021 has been published as the European harmonised accessibility standard. A reverification of the BPC must consider whether the 2010 citation should be retained, supplemented, or replaced. Counter-example same day: NZS 4121:2001 is 24 years old but remains the NZ Building Act §119 / D1/AS1 Acceptable Solution per NZ Ministry of Education March 2025 guidance; age does NOT predict supersession.

else:
    with scratch() as c:
        _before = c.execute("SELECT code_currency_status, code_currency_verified_at, code_currency_verified_by_session "
                            "FROM evidence_sources WHERE ref_id=?", (_ref27,)).fetchone()

        _row = c.execute("SELECT code_currency_status, code_currency_verified_at, code_currency_verified_by_session, "
                         "metadata_integrity_detail FROM evidence_sources WHERE ref_id=?", (_ref27,)).fetchone()
        record("T027-01", "amend-source sets code_currency_status to a member of the enum governance/tier-system.md ratifies, stamps "

        _rs = {"outside the enum": refusal(db.amend_source, _ref27, "code_currency_status", "CURRENT-ISH", "r", session=S, dry_run=True),

               "edition by hand": refusal(db.amend_source, _ref27, "edition", "2nd", "r", session=S, dry_run=True)}
        record("T027-03", "a value outside the enum is refused naming the enum; the stamp columns are not amendable; edition is a bibliographic "

===== v_research_scope
CREATE VIEW v_research_scope AS
-- v_research_scope: the (language, jurisdiction) pairs the research scope OWES a search for.
--
-- The ONE home of "what is owed": every lang_jur_map row not recorded `scoped-out`. A NULL scope_status is owed --
-- an unrecorded scope never shrinks the requirement (on 2026-11-06 marking four languages `scoped-out` left every
-- other row NULL, and `coverage` read required 0/0, complete true). The fill of scope_status is a data migration
-- after owner question 5; until then the requirement is the whole map, less what is recorded `scoped-out`.
-- Readers: v_coverage_priority, `db.py coverage`.
SELECT language, jurisdiction, role
  FROM lang_jur_map
 WHERE COALESCE(scope_status, 'in-scope') <> 'scoped-out'
===== v_coverage_priority
CREATE VIEW v_coverage_priority AS
SELECT
    s.slug,
    ljm.jurisdiction,
    ljm.language,
    ljm.role,
    ( (CASE ljm.role WHEN 'PRIMARY' THEN 3 ELSE 1 END)
      + (CASE WHEN (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM search_executions se2
                    WHERE se2.slug = s.slug AND se2.deferred_reason IS NULL) = 0
              THEN 2 ELSE 0 END)
    ) AS priority_score,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM search_executions se3
     WHERE se3.slug = s.slug AND se3.deferred_reason IS NULL) AS slug_searches
FROM slugs s
JOIN v_research_scope ljm        -- CROSS JOIN: every in-scope slug x every owed (lang,jur)
WHERE s.status IN ('ACTIVE', 'STUB')
  AND NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM search_executions se
      LEFT JOIN base_jurisdictions b ON b.jurisdiction_code = se.jurisdiction
      WHERE se.slug = s.slug
        AND COALESCE(b.parent_code, se.jurisdiction) = ljm.jurisdiction
        AND UPPER(se.language) = ljm.language
  )
===== v_scan_ledger
CREATE VIEW v_scan_ledger AS
-- v_scan_ledger: one row per (source in scope) x (active parameter).
--
--   source in scope   evidence_sources with superseded_by_ref_id IS NULL. A tombstone is
--                     never read again; its replacement is.
--   active parameter  base_parameters.status = 'active'. Retired and merged parameters
--                     leave the ledger (their extractions stay, as history).

--                        the quantity and sets nothing -- a positive statement.
--   3 READ-NOTHING-FOUND a FULL-scope reading covers the pair and found no row.
--   4 BLOCKED            no full reading covers the pair AND the source carries an obstacle
--                        processing_blocked_reason (below): the full text could not be
--                        obtained or read, so the pair is not reading debt until a full
--                        reading is recorded. Any partial / fragment / abstract reading of
--                        the pair is still named in scan_id / text_scope / method.
--   5 READ-PARTIAL       only partial / fragment / abstract readings cover it, and no
--                        obstacle stands: the full text is obtainable and unread -- debt.
--   6 NOT-READ           no reading covers it.

===== v_pending
CREATE VIEW v_pending AS
    SELECT ecs.*, g.description AS gap_description, g.category AS gap_category,
           g.priority AS gap_priority
    FROM "specifications" ecs
    JOIN gaps g ON g.gap_id = ecs.gap_register_id
    WHERE ecs.state = 'pending'
      AND ecs.retired_at IS NULL
===== v_gap_subject
CREATE VIEW v_gap_subject AS
    SELECT g.gap_id, g.parameter_id, g.identity_code, g.icf_code, g.needs_code, g.medical_code,
           g.jurisdiction, g.language, 'gaps' AS subject_home, NULL AS specification_id
      FROM gaps g
     WHERE COALESCE(g.parameter_id, g.identity_code, g.icf_code, g.needs_code, g.medical_code,
                    g.jurisdiction, g.language) IS NOT NULL
    UNION ALL
    SELECT g.gap_id, s.parameter_id, s.identity_code, s.icf_code, s.needs_code, s.medical_code,

                     ("needs_code", "access_needs", "need_code"), ("medical_code", "base_taxonomy_medical", "medical_code"))


def cell_status(parameter_id: int, identity: str = None, icf: str = None, needs: str = None,
                medical: str = None, jurisdiction: str = None, language: str = None) -> dict:
    """Where one cell stands, stage by stage, read from the tables and nothing else (T-034).

    For a parameter, and optionally a lens, a jurisdiction and a language, each stage reports four lists of
    row ids: `held` (what is there), `examined_empty` (looked at and found nothing), `never_examined` (not
    looked at) and `owed` (what the record says is still to be done). Every list is computed from the live
    tables and views (`v_research_scope`, `v_scan_ledger`, `v_live_lens_links`, ...), never typed, so a run
    started mid-pipeline can read what to skip and what to do. Read-only: nothing is written.

    A pair's scope is reported as it stands in `lang_jur_map.scope_status`: a NULL is reported as
    `scope_unrecorded` (owed, as `v_research_scope` reads it), never as in scope or out of it."""
    given = {"identity_code": identity, "icf_code": icf, "needs_code": needs, "medical_code": medical}
    lens = {k: v for k, v in given.items() if v}
    with connect(readonly=True) as conn:
        param = conn.execute("SELECT parameter_id, status FROM base_parameters WHERE parameter_id=?",
                             (parameter_id,)).fetchone()
        if param is None:
            raise Refusal(f"cell-status: parameter_id {parameter_id}: no such parameter. List them with SELECT "
                          f"parameter_id FROM base_parameters.")
        for col, tbl, key in _CELL_LENS_TABLES:
            if lens.get(col) and not dbcore.exists(conn, tbl, key, lens[col]):
                raise Refusal(f"cell-status: {col} {lens[col]!r} is not in {tbl}. List the codes with SELECT "
                              f"{key} FROM {tbl}.")
        ids = lambda sql, *a: [r[0] for r in conn.execute(sql, a)]          # noqa: E731
        lang = language.upper() if language else None
        # ---- research: the searches logged against this parameter, and the pairs the scope owes ----------
        pj = "COALESCE(b.parent_code, se.jurisdiction)"
        sfilter = ("se.parameter_id = ?" + (f" AND {pj} = ?" if jurisdiction else "")
                   + (" AND UPPER(se.language) = ?" if lang else ""))
        sargs = [parameter_id] + ([jurisdiction] if jurisdiction else []) + ([lang] if lang else [])
        base = ("SELECT se.exec_id FROM search_executions se LEFT JOIN base_jurisdictions b "
                "ON b.jurisdiction_code = se.jurisdiction WHERE " + sfilter)
        searched = {(r[0], r[1]) for r in conn.execute(
            f"SELECT UPPER(se.language), {pj} FROM search_executions se LEFT JOIN base_jurisdictions b "
            f"ON b.jurisdiction_code = se.jurisdiction WHERE {sfilter} AND se.deferred_reason IS NULL", sargs)}
        pairs = [dict(r) for r in conn.execute("SELECT language, jurisdiction, role, scope_status FROM lang_jur_map "
                                               "ORDER BY language, jurisdiction")
                 if (not jurisdiction or r["jurisdiction"] == jurisdiction) and (not lang or r["language"] == lang)]
        unsearched = [p for p in pairs if (p["language"], p["jurisdiction"]) not in searched]
        research = {
            "held": ids(base + " AND se.deferred_reason IS NULL AND COALESCE(se.results_admitted, 0) > 0", *sargs),
            "examined_empty": ids(base + " AND se.deferred_reason IS NULL AND COALESCE(se.results_admitted, 0) = 0", *sargs),
            "never_examined": {"deferred_searches": ids(base + " AND se.deferred_reason IS NOT NULL", *sargs),
                               "pairs_scoped_out": [f"{p['language']}/{p['jurisdiction']}" for p in unsearched
                                                    if p["scope_status"] == "scoped-out"]},
            "owed": {"pairs_in_scope": [f"{p['language']}/{p['jurisdiction']}" for p in unsearched
                                        if p["scope_status"] == "in-scope"],
                     "scope_unrecorded": [f"{p['language']}/{p['jurisdiction']}" for p in unsearched
                                          if p["scope_status"] is None]}}
        # ---- evidence and judgment: the extractions of this parameter, and the scan ledger ----------------
        ex_sql, ex_args = "SELECT e.extraction_id FROM source_value_extractions e WHERE e.parameter_id = ?", [parameter_id]
        if jurisdiction:
            ex_sql += " AND e.jurisdiction = ?"; ex_args.append(jurisdiction)
        for col, val in lens.items():
            ex_sql += (f" AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM v_live_lens_links l WHERE l.extraction_id = e.extraction_id "
                       f"AND l.{col} = ?)"); ex_args.append(val)
        extractions = ids(ex_sql + " ORDER BY e.extraction_id", *ex_args)
        scan = lambda *st: ids("SELECT ref_id FROM v_scan_ledger WHERE parameter_id = ? AND status IN (%s) ORDER BY ref_id"  # noqa: E731
                               % ",".join("?" * len(st)), parameter_id, *st)
        evidence = {"held": scan("EXTRACTED", "STATED-ABSENT"), "examined_empty": scan("READ-NOTHING-FOUND"),
                    "never_examined": scan("NOT-READ"), "owed": {"read_in_part_only": scan("READ-PARTIAL")}}
        qs = ",".join("?" * len(extractions)) or "NULL"
        judgment = {"held": extractions, "examined_empty": [], "never_examined": [],
                    "owed": {"open_follow_ups": ids(f"SELECT follow_up_id FROM extraction_follow_ups WHERE resolved_at "
                                                    f"IS NULL AND extraction_id IN ({qs}) ORDER BY follow_up_id", *extractions)}}
        # ---- synthesis: what weighs these figures together, and the gaps still open on the parameter -------
        synthesis = {"held": {"conflicts": ids("SELECT conflict_id FROM conflicts WHERE parameter_id = ? ORDER BY conflict_id", parameter_id),
                              "connections": ids("SELECT DISTINCT con_id FROM connection_targets WHERE parameter_id = ? ORDER BY con_id", parameter_id)},
                     "examined_empty": [], "never_examined": [],
                     "owed": {"open_gaps": ids("SELECT gap_id FROM gaps WHERE parameter_id = ? AND status LIKE 'OPEN%' ORDER BY gap_id", parameter_id)}}
        # ---- specification: the live determination(s) of the cell, their history, and the open gates ------
        sp = "SELECT specification_id FROM specifications WHERE parameter_id = ?" + "".join(f" AND {c} = ?" for c in lens)
        sp_args = [parameter_id, *lens.values()]
        gates = ids("SELECT gate_id FROM v_open_determination_gates WHERE parameter_id = ? ORDER BY gate_id", parameter_id)
        specification = {"held": [{"specification_id": r[0], "state": r[1]} for r in conn.execute(
                             sp.replace("SELECT specification_id", "SELECT specification_id, state")
                             + " AND retired_at IS NULL ORDER BY specification_id", sp_args)],
                         "retired": ids(sp + " AND retired_at IS NOT NULL ORDER BY specification_id", *sp_args),
                         "examined_empty": [], "never_examined": [], "owed": {"open_gates": gates}}
    return {"parameter_id": parameter_id, "parameter_status": param["status"], "lens": lens,
            "jurisdiction": jurisdiction, "language": lang,
            "stages": {"research": research, "evidence": evidence, "judgment": judgment, "synthesis": synthesis,
                       "specification": specification},
            "note": "Lists are row ids read from the live tables. `scope_unrecorded` pairs are owed until a scope is "
                    "recorded (set-pair-scope); render holds no rows of its own."}

import pathlib
p=pathlib.Path('scripts/db.py'); t=p.read_text()
def sub(a,b):
    global t; assert t.count(a)==1,a[:60]; t=t.replace(a,b)
func='''_CELL_LENS_TABLES = (("identity_code", "base_taxonomy_identity", "identity_code"), ("icf_code", "base_icf", "icf_code"),
                     ("needs_code", "access_needs", "need_code"), ("medical_code", "base_taxonomy_medical", "medical_code"))


def cell_status(parameter_id: int, identity: str = None, icf: str = None, needs: str = None,
                medical: str = None, jurisdiction: str = None, language: str = None) -> dict:
    """Where one cell stands, stage by stage, read from the tables and nothing else (T-034).

    For a parameter, and optionally a lens, a jurisdiction and a language, each stage reports four lists of
    row ids: `held` (what is there), `examined_empty` (looked at and found nothing), `never_examined` (not
    looked at) and `owed` (what the record says is still to be done). Every list is computed from the live
    tables and views (`v_research_scope`, `v_scan_ledger`, `v_live_lens_links`, ...), never typed, so a run
    started mid-pipeline can read what to skip and what to do. Read-only: nothing is written.

    A pair's scope is reported as it stands in `lang_jur_map.scope_status`: a NULL is reported as
    `scope_unrecorded` (owed, as `v_research_scope` reads it), never as in scope or out of it."""
    given = {"identity_code": identity, "icf_code": icf, "needs_code": needs, "medical_code": medical}
    lens = {k: v for k, v in given.items() if v}
    with connect(readonly=True) as conn:
        param = conn.execute("SELECT parameter_id, status FROM base_parameters WHERE parameter_id=?",
                             (parameter_id,)).fetchone()
        if param is None:
            raise Refusal(f"cell-status: parameter_id {parameter_id}: no such parameter. List them with SELECT "
                          f"parameter_id FROM base_parameters.")
        for col, tbl, key in _CELL_LENS_TABLES:
            if lens.get(col) and not dbcore.exists(conn, tbl, key, lens[col]):
                raise Refusal(f"cell-status: {col} {lens[col]!r} is not in {tbl}. List the codes with SELECT "
                              f"{key} FROM {tbl}.")
        ids = lambda sql, *a: [r[0] for r in conn.execute(sql, a)]          # noqa: E731
        lang = language.upper() if language else None
        # ---- research: the searches logged against this parameter, and the pairs the scope owes ----------
        pj = "COALESCE(b.parent_code, se.jurisdiction)"
        sfilter = ("se.parameter_id = ?" + (f" AND {pj} = ?" if jurisdiction else "")
                   + (" AND UPPER(se.language) = ?" if lang else ""))
        sargs = [parameter_id] + ([jurisdiction] if jurisdiction else []) + ([lang] if lang else [])
        base = ("SELECT se.exec_id FROM search_executions se LEFT JOIN base_jurisdictions b "
                "ON b.jurisdiction_code = se.jurisdiction WHERE " + sfilter)
        searched = {(r[0], r[1]) for r in conn.execute(
            f"SELECT UPPER(se.language), {pj} FROM search_executions se LEFT JOIN base_jurisdictions b "
            f"ON b.jurisdiction_code = se.jurisdiction WHERE {sfilter} AND se.deferred_reason IS NULL", sargs)}
        pairs = [dict(r) for r in conn.execute("SELECT language, jurisdiction, role, scope_status FROM lang_jur_map "
                                               "ORDER BY language, jurisdiction")
                 if (not jurisdiction or r["jurisdiction"] == jurisdiction) and (not lang or r["language"] == lang)]
        unsearched = [p for p in pairs if (p["language"], p["jurisdiction"]) not in searched]
        research = {
            "held": ids(base + " AND se.deferred_reason IS NULL AND COALESCE(se.results_admitted, 0) > 0", *sargs),
            "examined_empty": ids(base + " AND se.deferred_reason IS NULL AND COALESCE(se.results_admitted, 0) = 0", *sargs),
            "never_examined": {"deferred_searches": ids(base + " AND se.deferred_reason IS NOT NULL", *sargs),
                               "pairs_scoped_out": [f"{p['language']}/{p['jurisdiction']}" for p in unsearched
                                                    if p["scope_status"] == "scoped-out"]},
            "owed": {"pairs_in_scope": [f"{p['language']}/{p['jurisdiction']}" for p in unsearched
                                        if p["scope_status"] == "in-scope"],
                     "scope_unrecorded": [f"{p['language']}/{p['jurisdiction']}" for p in unsearched
                                          if p["scope_status"] is None]}}
        # ---- evidence and judgment: the extractions of this parameter, and the scan ledger ----------------
        ex_sql, ex_args = "SELECT e.extraction_id FROM source_value_extractions e WHERE e.parameter_id = ?", [parameter_id]
        if jurisdiction:
            ex_sql += " AND e.jurisdiction = ?"; ex_args.append(jurisdiction)
        for col, val in lens.items():
            ex_sql += (f" AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM v_live_lens_links l WHERE l.extraction_id = e.extraction_id "
                       f"AND l.{col} = ?)"); ex_args.append(val)
        extractions = ids(ex_sql + " ORDER BY e.extraction_id", *ex_args)
        scan = lambda *st: ids("SELECT ref_id FROM v_scan_ledger WHERE parameter_id = ? AND status IN (%s) ORDER BY ref_id"  # noqa: E731
                               % ",".join("?" * len(st)), parameter_id, *st)
        evidence = {"held": scan("EXTRACTED", "STATED-ABSENT"), "examined_empty": scan("READ-NOTHING-FOUND"),
                    "never_examined": scan("NOT-READ"), "owed": {"read_in_part_only": scan("READ-PARTIAL")}}
        qs = ",".join("?" * len(extractions)) or "NULL"
        judgment = {"held": extractions, "examined_empty": [], "never_examined": [],
                    "owed": {"open_follow_ups": ids(f"SELECT follow_up_id FROM extraction_follow_ups WHERE resolved_at "
                                                    f"IS NULL AND extraction_id IN ({qs}) ORDER BY follow_up_id", *extractions)}}
        # ---- synthesis: what weighs these figures together, and the gaps still open on the parameter -------
        synthesis = {"held": {"conflicts": ids("SELECT conflict_id FROM conflicts WHERE parameter_id = ? ORDER BY conflict_id", parameter_id),
                              "connections": ids("SELECT DISTINCT con_id FROM connection_targets WHERE parameter_id = ? ORDER BY con_id", parameter_id)},
                     "examined_empty": [], "never_examined": [],
                     "owed": {"open_gaps": ids("SELECT gap_id FROM gaps WHERE parameter_id = ? AND status LIKE 'OPEN%' ORDER BY gap_id", parameter_id)}}
        # ---- specification: the live determination(s) of the cell, their history, and the open gates ------
        sp = "SELECT specification_id FROM specifications WHERE parameter_id = ?" + "".join(f" AND {c} = ?" for c in lens)
        sp_args = [parameter_id, *lens.values()]
        gates = ids("SELECT gate_id FROM v_open_determination_gates WHERE parameter_id = ? ORDER BY gate_id", parameter_id)
        specification = {"held": [{"specification_id": r[0], "state": r[1]} for r in conn.execute(
                             sp.replace("SELECT specification_id", "SELECT specification_id, state")
                             + " AND retired_at IS NULL ORDER BY specification_id", sp_args)],
                         "retired": ids(sp + " AND retired_at IS NOT NULL ORDER BY specification_id", *sp_args),
                         "examined_empty": [], "never_examined": [], "owed": {"open_gates": gates}}
    return {"parameter_id": parameter_id, "parameter_status": param["status"], "lens": lens,
            "jurisdiction": jurisdiction, "language": lang,
            "stages": {"research": research, "evidence": evidence, "judgment": judgment, "synthesis": synthesis,
                       "specification": specification},
            "note": "Lists are row ids read from the live tables. `scope_unrecorded` pairs are owed until a scope is "
                    "recorded (set-pair-scope); render holds no rows of its own."}


'''

Read-only throughout. `sha256sum data/guidebook.db` was `ffb77371…a723` before and after. All writers ran on copies under `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-guidebook/a9452ae4-7ff6-5ee7-9d22-5a8cc7e0001d/scratchpad/crit/` (called `$S` below). HEAD moved to cb7e75a9 (T-027) while I worked; I attacked the three named commits only.

Twelve findings (F1 to F12), ranked worst first, then the attacks that found nothing.

---

## F1. HIGH (T-021): a QUESTION is not visible in anything the engine prints or emits

- **Artefact:** `/home/user/guidebook/scripts/assess/assess_cell.py`: `derivation_handshake` (QUESTION branch, about line 673) and the `report.append({k: det[k] for k in (...)})` key list in `main` (about line 2396).
- **Claim:** the commit says the engine "reports a QUESTION beside the cell". The task's AT-72 says "see the cell flagged in the engine report". OD-21 ACTION (2) says "Show the cell as questioned".
- **Failure:** `"gates"` is absent from the report key list. It is not in stdout, not in `--emit-sql`, not in `--report-json`. The QUESTION lives only in `determine()`'s return dict.
- **Why the tests pass:** T021-01..05 assert on that dict (`d["gates"]`), which is how "the cell's report carries the question" is green.
- **Command:** on two copies of the live DB, one with `db.py raise-determination-gate --parameter-id 3 --identity MOB --verdict QUESTION --detail "TASK-FIXTURE …"`, I ran `assess_cell.py --db … --parameter-id 3 --identity MOB --slug aac-speech-production-environments --stamp '2026-11-15 22:00' --report-json …` on each.
  - stdout, the SQL artefact and the report JSON were byte-identical between the two runs.
  - `grep -c -i "question\|long-cane" q1.out q1.sql q1.json` printed 0.
- **Compounding:** a live determination cannot be re-run ("already determined" refusal), so for a cell that is actually published the engine never reads the gate at all.
- **Early return:** `derivation_handshake` returns `[]` gates for a cell with no sources and no function path, so a QUESTION there is dropped even from the dict.

## F2. HIGH (T-025): all four verbs write on ledger entries that are not the owner's

- **Artefact:** `/home/user/guidebook/scripts/db.py`, `_owner_approval` (about line 8590 at 15689962).
- **Claim:** commit: "each pointing at one dated owner entry". Docstring: "one dated ledger entry, and the owner's own". Task: "No verb here writes without an owner entry to point at".
- **Failure:** the only exclusion is `heading.startswith("Delegated resolution")`. Every other dated, unique heading passes.
- **Commands (scratch `t25.db`, all returned a result and wrote the row):**
  - `add-identity --code ZZFIX …` on `## Referral 2026-11-13 — OD-44 …` (a question referred to the owner, unanswered).
  - `add-identity --code ZZKID --parent MOB …` on `## Correction 2026-11-12 — to the delegated resolution of OD-14, the rows written under MOB: withdrawn and referred back to the owner`. An entry that withdraws a model's resolution on the MOB split admitted a child of MOB.
  - `add-lang-jur-pair --language XX --jurisdiction US …` on `## Supersession record 2026-11-15 …`, whose own DATE line says "not a new owner statement". Result: `new_language: true`.
  - `set-pair-scope --language EN --jurisdiction US --scope-status scoped-out` on the Referral.
  - `amend-identity --code MOB --display-name …` on the Referral: MOB's display name was replaced.
- **Size of the hole:** 40 of 193 dated unique headings neither start "Owner" nor are refused. Re-derive, do not trust: the `_heads` expression at `scripts/tests/test_run_pipeline_refusals.py` lines 992 to 995, filtered on `not h.startswith("Owner")`.
- **The test proves it:** `_OWNER_H` (line 994) resolves on the live ledger to `Session 2026-04-06 — Evidence Expansion Phase 1 (CO-0005)`. Every "legitimate" T025 case is green on a session heading, under a section titled "each pointing at an owner entry".
- **Not covered by the task's accepted limitation:** that limitation is that the entry may not approve *this act*. Here the entry is not an owner entry at all, which the commit added a check for and claims to hold.

## F3. MEDIUM-HIGH (T-021): the committed database does not carry the DDL the committed migration produces

- **Artefact:** `/home/user/guidebook/scripts/migrations/133_gate_question.sql` line 30 against `sqlite_master.sql` of `determination_gates` in the committed `data/guidebook.db`.
- **Claim:** "rebuild reproduces the database, migration_reproducibility --deep PASS".
- **Failure:** the committed DB's table comment reads "A gate that names several lens columns applies to a cell that carries ALL of them." The committed migration reads "A gate is skipped for a cell only when the cell carries a DIFFERENT code in a lens the gate names; …". The file was edited after it was applied (rule 3: immutable once applied).
- **The comment in the live schema is false:** the engine applies an ICF-keyed gate to a cell that carries no ICF code (see F5).
- **Command:** `python3 scripts/migrate_db.py --rebuild $S/rebuilt.db` (rc 0), then diff `select name, sql from sqlite_master` between it and `data/guidebook.db`: `SCHEMA TEXT DIFFERS: determination_gates`.
- **The gate cited could not see it:** `migration_reproducibility.py --deep` printed PASS, "59 tables identical". It compares rows, not schema text.

## F4. MEDIUM (T-023): a ninth owner sentence sits inside the run and is in the ledger nowhere; it is the antecedent of O3

- **Artefact:** `/home/user/guidebook/transcripts/harness_db856d85/main.jsonl` line 4865 (enqueue, `2026-10-12T02:05:02.301Z`) and line 4874 (attachment `queued_command`, origin human): "upon completion, perform a comparative analysis between workplan v2 and ideal state graph".
- **Failure:** it falls between O2 (01:54:09) and O3 (02:05:50), 48 seconds before O3's "wherever there is a conflict, adjudicate…". O3's "conflict" is between workplan v2 and the ideal graph. The entry presents O3 without it.
- **Why the search missed it:** the `DECISION-CLOSURE.md` §2 command filters on the eight relay patterns, so it could not have returned a ninth.
- **Command:** `grep -c -F "perform a comparative analysis between workplan v2" references/project-standards.md` prints 0. I also listed every human-origin line of 2026-10-12 between 00:00 and 03:30.

## F5. MEDIUM (T-021): the lens-matching rule is stated three ways, and the one the operator reads is false

- **Engine and migration file:** a gate is skipped only when the cell carries a different code in a lens the gate names.
- **`db.py` help (`--icf`, `--needs`, `--medical`, about line 2283):** "gate only cells that carry this ICF code".
- **Committed DB comment:** "applies to a cell that carries ALL of them".
- **Failure:** a binding gate raised with `--icf` caps identity-only cells that carry no ICF lens.
- **Command:** `$S/eng.py` on the pilot fixture: a `MISLINKED` T1 gate with `icf_code` only, cell `{"identity_code": "MOB"}`, gives `state=provisional, binds=True`.
- T021-04 asserts this behaviour for questions, so it is deliberate. The help and the stored DDL contradict it.

## F6. MEDIUM (T-021): the owner's page labels a gate keyed on ICF, need or medical code as "every lens"

- **Artefact:** `/home/user/guidebook/governance/owner-browser.yaml`, `open_gates` (about line 1119): `coalesce(identity_code, 'every lens')`.
- **Status:** the file is in the task's own hit list and the commit did not touch it.
- **Command:** on scratch `q1.db` with a `--icf b114` QUESTION, the page's SQL returns `'parameter 3 · every lens · QUESTION'` beside `icf_code='b114'`.
- **Same block, also wrong for a QUESTION:**
  - glossary (line 56): "raised … when new evidence may overturn it";
  - `why_yours`: "a determination may rest on the wrong evidence";
  - the hand-written option "Resolve it: the abstract overstated".
  OD-21 says "questioned, not wrong".
- **Second prose caller left behind:** `/home/user/guidebook/governance/evidence-architecture.md` line 145, "Gate rows carry the tier and type of the triggering source", is now false for QUESTION rows.

## F7. MEDIUM (T-025): the T025 cases stay green with seven refusals or writes removed

- **Method:** one mutation per tree copy at 15689962, `scripts/tests/test_run_pipeline_refusals.py` run on each. Baseline "PASS: all 398". Driver: `$S/mut.py`; outputs: `$S/out_mt_*.txt`.
- **Still "PASS: all 398" with:**
  - **A.** The date check deleted from `require_approval_heading`. T025-03's "no date" probe passes for the wrong reason: the ref is the literal `'no date here'`, the message echoes it, and the assertion is `"no date" in msg`. T-024's T024-01 has the same shape (`test_db_amend_writers.py` about line 2404). Only `test_scan_contract` M05b goes red, and only for mint.
  - **B.** The delegated check removed from `set-pair-scope` and `amend-identity` (tested only on `add-lang-jur-pair` and `add-identity`).
  - **C.** `--parent` accepted whatever its status (no deprecated code exists live; no fixture built).
  - **D.** A code containing a space accepted.
  - **E.** A blank `--description` accepted.
  - **F.** `amend-identity --category` not checked against the CHECK.
  - **M.** `add-identity` not writing `description` at all. T025-06's title says "with its name, category, description and stamps" and never reads the column.
- **Went red as they should:** jurisdiction check, role check, scope-status check, category check on add, delegated check on the two tested verbs, blank amend value, unchanged-value rewrite.
- **Commit's own seeded defects:** it reports two (no delegated check, no held-pair check). I confirmed the delegated one; I did not re-run the held-pair one.
- **Never exercised with a non-NULL value:** `amend-identity --description`/`--category` and `set-pair-scope … scoped-out`.

## F8. MEDIUM, latent (T-025): `add-lang-jur-pair` admits a pair that no search can ever satisfy

- **Artefact:** `add_lang_jur_pair` (`dbcore.check_jurisdiction` accepts any held code) against `v_coverage_priority` and `db.py coverage`, which match a search under `COALESCE(parent_code, se.jurisdiction)`.
- **Failure:** a pair keyed on a sub-national code is owed by every ACTIVE/STUB slug, and a search logged under that code is matched to the parent, so the pair never leaves the unsearched list.
- **Command:** scratch `sub.db` with a fixture row `US-TFX` (sub-national, parent US), then `add-lang-jur-pair --language EN --jurisdiction US-TFX --role PRIMARY`. Accepted. `v_coverage_priority` then lists the pair for all 103 active/stub slugs, and a `US-TFX` search is matched under `US`.
- **Why latent:** no sub-national code is held today (`select count(*) from base_jurisdictions where kind='sub-national'`).
- **Related by design, not a defect:** any admitted pair is owed at once (NULL reads as in-scope).

## F9. MEDIUM (T-023): "What they record" says more, and less, than the quotes

- **Artefact:** `/home/user/guidebook/references/project-standards.md`, the new entry (from line 7631), paragraph "What they record" and the heading.
- **More than the quotes:**
  - "across tables that carry references and ids" narrows O7's "across all tables with references and ids": it drops "all" and resolves an ambiguous "with" restrictively.
  - The heading and paragraph assign all eight to "the idealized state graph". O4 to O8 do not name it, and O3 concerns the comparison (F4).
- **Less than the quotes:** O1's "dynamically scrape mine organize and sort all relevant information from any source for any parameter regardless of search slug" and O3's "100% accuracy, code compliance" are absent from the summary.
- The entry's own ACTION (2) forbids reading a further meaning into a sentence.

## F10. LOW-MEDIUM (T-023): the entry misquotes the ledger line it cites, inside quotation marks

- **Artefact:** line 7633 quotes `"OD-28: enter the eight sentences verbatim from the committed transcript"` as what "the owner answered".
- **Actual:** the ledger line (5976) reads "OD-28: enter the eight sentences of 2026-10-12 verbatim from the committed transcript". The owner's selection (5975) was "Enter them verbatim from the transcript".
- **Command:** `grep -c -F 'OD-28: enter the eight sentences verbatim from the committed transcript' references/project-standards.md` prints 1, and that one is the new entry itself.

## F11. LOW (T-021): the `--medical` path and the audit's new branches have examined nothing

- `base_taxonomy_medical` holds 0 rows, so in T021-06 `_MED` is `None`. The case "names the lens codes it was given" was given no medical code.
- `derivation_handshake_integrity` on the canonical DB prints `determinations: 0 … EXAMINED: 1`. The QUESTION skip and the four-lens match have never executed there, and no committed case covers them.
- On my scratch `q1.db` (one live determination, two open QUESTIONs) the audit ran CLEAN without crashing.

## F12. LOW (T-021 and T-025): smaller items

- `raise-determination-gate --verdict QUESTION` accepts a parameter with no live determination. All eight `specifications` rows are retired and my raise on parameter 3 succeeded. It is "a question about a published cell" with no published cell.
- An open QUESTION blocks `retire-parameter` and `merge-parameter` (`_refuse_live_work`), because any open gate does.
- The delegated-prefix refusal now has two homes: inline in `add_jurisdiction` and in `_owner_approval`. `mint_term_from_catalogue` still strips `## ` itself before calling the helper, which strips it again.
- The new verbs stamp `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM` into columns whose existing rows hold ISO-8601 with offset (`base_taxonomy_identity.created_at`, `lang_jur_map.created_at`).

---

## Attacks that found nothing

- `[NULL: engine capping or crashing on a QUESTION — examined, nothing found]` Covered: QUESTION with no lens, identity, icf, needs, medical, resolved, two at once, beside a binding gate, beside a non-binding T5 gate, an empty-string lens, and the real `determine` path. It never caps and never crashes. A non-QUESTION with a NULL tier does crash (`TypeError`), but the CHECK makes that unreachable.
- `[NULL: the CHECK — examined, nothing found]` Hand-INSERTs on a copy: QUESTION with a tier, an evidence type or a source is refused. Every other verdict without both tier and evidence type is refused. Bad lens FKs are refused. The resolved triple still holds.
- `[NULL: migration 133 preserving data — examined, nothing found]` Gate 1 is identical column for column to `31c40d7a~1`. `sqlite_sequence` stays at 1 and the next id is 2. `idx_gates_open` is identical. There are six FKs (three old, three new). No table references the gate table. `foreign_key_check` is empty and `integrity_check` is ok. No table's row count moved. Only two schema objects changed. `joined_cells_census` gives 66 candidates before and after.
- `[NULL: old identity rule against the new rule — examined, nothing found]` For an identity-only gate the new predicate reduces to the old `g[6] and identity and g[6] != identity`.
- `[NULL: readers assuming a non-NULL tier — examined, nothing found]` `owner_browser_build.py` does not read the tier. The audit formats it only after the QUESTION skip. The resolve verb works on a QUESTION (T021-10).
- `[NULL: T-023 quotes and timestamps — examined, nothing found]` All eight equal the decoded transcript text. O1 and O3 each differ only by one trailing space, which was dropped. Each timestamp is that of the line described:
  - O1 to O3 are the enqueue lines 4579, 4601 and 4906. They have no delivered `user` line; origin human is on the `queued_command` attachment lines 4583, 4603 and 4911.
  - O4 to O8 are the `user` lines 4931, 4950, 4965, 4976 and 4991, origin `{'kind': 'human'}`, not sidechain.
- `[NULL: T-023 touching other ledger lines — examined, nothing found]` `git diff 26ba3b2c~1 26ba3b2c --numstat` gives `42 0`. `supersession_backpointer_audit` is PASS, EXAMINED 12.
- `[NULL: helper call point and words — examined, nothing found]` "no date" and "exactly one" are kept. `test_scan_contract` M05, M05b, M05c, M05d and M05e are green at 15689962. With the helper call removed from mint, M05, M05b, M05c, M05d and M05e's sibling M07 go red (the "XX" line in my tree is my own exclusion artefact). T024-01..32 are green in the real repo.
- `[NULL: stored values changing under the helper — examined, nothing found]` Mint stripped `## ` before and after. `add_jurisdiction`'s strip only moved past checks that do not read the ref. Live rows cannot show this: 0 `terms.catalogue_approval_ref` and 0 `base_jurisdictions.admission_ref` are populated, so the proof is code plus M07 and T024-20.
- `[NULL: T-025 result keys, flags and captured set — examined, nothing found]` Result keys match section 4 for all four verbs. `new_language` is true and false as specified. `scope_status` is written NULL. The evidence command no longer lists `lang_jur_map` or `base_taxonomy_identity`.
- **Not attacked:** T024 cases under the "helper removed from add-jurisdiction" mutation. My mutation tree lacks `transcripts/` and that test file aborts earlier. `test_run_pipeline_refusals` stayed all-green under that mutation.
- **Out of scope, seen in passing:** T027-01 is red at the current HEAD (cb7e75a9).

def scratch():
    """A second copy of the test database for a case that needs hand-built state (each such
    statement says HAND), with its own copy of the scratch retrieval log: a source minted on the copy
    takes an id the main copy will mint too, and the two must not hold each other's files. db.py follows
    GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH and GUIDEBOOK_RETRIEVAL_LOG at call time, so its writers act on the copies."""
    k = next(_scratches)
    path = os.path.join(TMP, f"scratch-{k}.db")
    shutil.copy(DB, path)
    root = os.path.join(TMP, f"scratch-log-{k}")
    os.makedirs(root)
    for e in pathlib.Path(retrieval_log.LOG_ROOT).iterdir():
        if e.is_symlink():
            os.symlink(os.readlink(e), os.path.join(root, e.name))
        elif e.is_dir():
            shutil.copytree(e, os.path.join(root, e.name))
    old_root = retrieval_log.LOG_ROOT
    os.environ["GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH"], os.environ["GUIDEBOOK_RETRIEVAL_LOG"] = path, root
    retrieval_log.DB_PATH, retrieval_log.LOG_ROOT = pathlib.Path(path), pathlib.Path(root)
    retrieval_log._ARTEFACT_INDEX.clear()
    c = sqlite3.connect(path)
    c.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    try:
        yield c
    finally:
        c.close()
        os.environ["GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH"], os.environ["GUIDEBOOK_RETRIEVAL_LOG"] = DB, str(old_root)
        retrieval_log.DB_PATH, retrieval_log.LOG_ROOT = pathlib.Path(DB), old_root
CREATE TABLE base_jurisdictions (
    -- THE SHAPE OF A CODE, held by the table where a table can hold it: upper-case letters,
    -- digits and at most one dash, with a letter first; the GB prefix is the ruled rejected
    -- spelling (UK is the project's code). The dash belongs to a sub-national code and to
    -- no other kind, and a sub-national code is exactly <parent_code>-<a non-empty
    -- subdivision>. That the parent is a `country` cannot be a CHECK (it reads another
    -- row); the writer, db.py add-jurisdiction, refuses it.
    jurisdiction_code  TEXT PRIMARY KEY
                       CHECK (jurisdiction_code = UPPER(jurisdiction_code)

def scratch():
    """A second copy of the test database for a case that needs hand-built state (each such
    statement says HAND), with its own copy of the scratch retrieval log: a source minted on the copy
    takes an id the main copy will mint too, and the two must not hold each other's files. db.py follows
    GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH and GUIDEBOOK_RETRIEVAL_LOG at call time, so its writers act on the copies."""
    k = next(_scratches)
    path = os.path.join(TMP, f"scratch-{k}.db")
    shutil.copy(DB, path)
    root = os.path.join(TMP, f"scratch-log-{k}")
    os.makedirs(root)
    for e in pathlib.Path(retrieval_log.LOG_ROOT).iterdir():
        if e.is_symlink():
            os.symlink(os.readlink(e), os.path.join(root, e.name))
        elif e.is_dir():
            shutil.copytree(e, os.path.join(root, e.name))
    old_root = retrieval_log.LOG_ROOT
    os.environ["GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH"], os.environ["GUIDEBOOK_RETRIEVAL_LOG"] = path, root
    retrieval_log.DB_PATH, retrieval_log.LOG_ROOT = pathlib.Path(path), pathlib.Path(root)
    retrieval_log._ARTEFACT_INDEX.clear()
    c = sqlite3.connect(path)
    c.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    try:
        yield c
    finally:
        c.close()
        os.environ["GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH"], os.environ["GUIDEBOOK_RETRIEVAL_LOG"] = DB, str(old_root)
        retrieval_log.DB_PATH, retrieval_log.LOG_ROOT = pathlib.Path(DB), old_root

    -- THE SHAPE OF A CODE, held by the table where a table can hold it: upper-case letters,
    -- digits and at most one dash, with a letter first; the GB prefix is the ruled rejected
    -- spelling (UK is the project's code). The dash belongs to a sub-national code and to
    -- no other kind, and a sub-national code is exactly <parent_code>-<a non-empty
    -- subdivision>. That the parent is a `country` cannot be a CHECK (it reads another
    -- row); the writer, db.py add-jurisdiction, refuses it.

                              AND jurisdiction_code NOT LIKE 'GB%'

content.content:
## 2. Preconditions

- **The integration base.** This workplan must be on the branch you start from. If the workplan's pull request is merged, that is `origin/main`. Until then it is the workplan branch, `origin/ccr-408aaa9b-z3e4s0` (if that name is gone: `git branch -r --contains "$(git log --all --format=%H -1 -- workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN.md)"`). Every command in this file uses `$BASE`, set by the first line of the set-up block, and never a literal `origin/main`: on a base that lacks the workplan, a diff against `origin/main` contains the whole workplan and every gate and count is about the wrong change.
- **Tasks that must be merged to the integration base first:** none. Check by running that task's own after-test (its section 6), or `git log "$BASE" --oneline | grep -F "<that task's commit subject>"`.
- **Owner decisions that must be answered first.** The answer must be in `references/project-standards.md` (the ledger), in the owner's words.
  - **OD-37** — answered by the owner, 2026-11-12 (third set): "MOVE and VES are access needs, agreed." (`grep -n -F "OD-37: identity-lens rule" references/project-standards.md`). Check: `grep -F "OD-37 STATUS:" references/project-standards.md | tail -1` must read `ANSWERED BY THE OWNER`.
- **Tests that must be red (or green) before you start:** `base_taxonomy_identity` has no column naming the need a retired identity code went to, and no verb retires one.
- **Set-up.**


## 3. The problem, in the guidebook's terms

`MOVE` (movement disorders) and `VES` (vestibular disorders) sit in the identity registry as populations, though the owner has agreed they are access needs, and the needs that carry them already exist (`A-PRECISION` absorbs movement disorders, `A-STABLE` vestibular disorders). Nothing can retire an identity code and say where its readers should go instead, so a writer given `MOVE` still accepts it as an identity.

**Evidence command** (read-only):

```
python3 -I -c "import sqlite3;c=sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro',uri=True);print([r[1] for r in c.execute('pragma table_info(base_taxonomy_identity)')]);print(c.execute(\"select identity_code,status,description from base_taxonomy_identity where identity_code in ('MOVE','VES')\").fetchall());print(c.execute(\"select need_code,absorbs from access_needs where need_code in ('A-PRECISION','A-STABLE')\").fetchall())"
python3 -I -c "import sqlite3;c=sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro',uri=True);T=[t for (t,) in c.execute(\"select name from sqlite_master where type='table'\")];print({t+'.'+r[1]:c.execute('select count(*) from \"'+t+'\" where \"'+r[1]+'\" in (?,?)',('MOVE','VES')).fetchone()[0] for t in T for r in c.execute('pragma table_info(\"'+t+'\")') if r[1] in ('identity_code','target_population','pop_a','pop_b','parent_code')})"
```

**Expected output today:** no column for a successor need; both codes `active`; both needs present; every identity-bearing column holds 0 rows of either code (only the registry rows name them). If the output differs, the ground has moved: stop (section 9).

## 4. The change

Order of preference, from CLAUDE.md §8: do nothing and say why; change a rule or convention; reuse what exists; delete the cause; only then add the smallest code that closes the defect.

1. Schema migration: `base_taxonomy_identity.superseded_by_need TEXT REFERENCES access_needs(need_code)`, with a CHECK that it is set only when `status = 'deprecated'`. Create, copy, drop, rename; recreate every view and index that names the table (`select type, name from sqlite_master where sql like '%base_taxonomy_identity%'`). Never type the migration number: derive it (`ls scripts/migrations | grep -E '^[0-9]{3}_' | sort | tail -1`, plus one), and end it by setting `PRAGMA user_version` to it. Run `python3 scripts/audit/joined_cells_census.py` before and after; apply only with `python3 scripts/migrate_db.py`; prove with `python3 scripts/migrate_db.py --rebuild "$SCRATCH/rebuilt.db"` and `python3 scripts/audit/migration_reproducibility.py --deep`.
1a. **[Added 2026-11-12, OI-13 fold] The identity successor, in the same migration.** Also add `base_taxonomy_identity.superseded_by_identity TEXT REFERENCES base_taxonomy_identity(identity_code)`, and make the CHECK: a deprecated row has **exactly one** successor column set, an active row none (T-056 later adds a third successor column and widens this CHECK; it does not add a second mechanism). One mechanism serves both cases the owner's answers need: `SCI` retires to `WHEEL` (T-102) and `LMB` retires to `UPL` (T-116). A rename of the code was rejected: `identity_code` is a key other rows point at, and the 2026-09-16 ruling retires identifiers in place.
1b. **[Added 2026-11-12, OI-13 fold] Crossing-map rows retire in place.** `identity_icf_map` gains `retired_at`, `retired_by_session` and `retired_reason` (all NULL on a live row; a CHECK that the three are set together), and one verb `retire-population-icf-link --link-id N --reason "..." --session S`. Without it the refusal of item 2 is a dead end: `SCI` and `LMB` carry crossing rows (`select identity_code, count(*) from identity_icf_map where identity_code in ('SCI','LMB') group by 1`), and no verb removes or retires one. A crossing moves to a successor as a new row through the existing `add-population-icf-link` (its provenance names the old `link_id`) followed by retiring the old row; the table's `UNIQUE (identity_code, icf_code, mechanism)` already refuses a duplicate on the successor. A retired crossing is never un-retired. Every reader of `identity_icf_map` filters `retired_at IS NULL` first (the 2026-09-16 ruling's execution condition): find them with `git grep -n identity_icf_map -- scripts skills ':!scripts/migrations'` and `select name from sqlite_master where sql like '%identity_icf_map%'`.
2. One verb, `retire-identity --code (--need N | --to-identity C) --approval-ref H --reason R`, where `H` is the full text of a dated `## ` heading of `references/project-standards.md` found exactly once (corrected 2026-11-13 from a quoted ledger pointer: the one approval-pointer shape that T-024's `add-jurisdiction` and T-025's identity and pair verbs take for base admissions; T-025 section 4 names the check, `dbcore.require_approval_heading`; T-054 has no dependency on T-025, so it checks inline with `dbcore.ledger_heading_count`, as `add-jurisdiction` does today, and T-025's sweep converts that inline check to the helper when it merges. Chosen 2026-11-13, to avoid serialising T-054, T-056, T-114 and T-115 behind T-025), checked and printed in the result, not stored: sets `status = 'deprecated'` and `superseded_by_need`; never deletes. It refuses a code that any live row still carries (every column that takes an identity code, derived from the foreign keys into `base_taxonomy_identity`, not listed), naming the count and T-114's re-tag as the next action; and refuses a need that does not exist.
3. Every writer that takes an identity code refuses a `deprecated` one, and its message names the successor to use instead (read from whichever successor column is set). **Live rows** for the refusal of item 2 are rows with no retirement mark where the table has one (`identity_icf_map.retired_at`, and after T-018 `extraction_lens_links.retired_at`); `--to-identity` refuses a successor that is deprecated, is the code itself, or does not exist. `evidence_population_match.target_population` takes identity codes but has no foreign key, so the derivation by foreign keys misses it: name it explicitly in the refusal's message as a table to re-grade by judgment (never fan out a grade) and make `add-population-match` refuse a deprecated target like the other writers. Readers of `superseded_by_identity`: these refusal messages, and T-102 and T-116, which call the verb. Find the writers by the foreign keys and by the existing "LIVE code, not a retired one" help strings in `scripts/db.py`; locate by symbol.
4. Caller in scope: `governance/population-taxonomy.md`'s list of identity codes gains one note that `MOVE` and `VES` are retired to their needs by T-114; change nothing else there.

**What reads what this task adds or changes:** every writer that takes an identity code; the lens switch; `/run-pipeline`; T-114.

**Code size.** Report `git diff --shortstat "$(git merge-base HEAD "$BASE")" -- scripts schemas .github skills ':!scripts/migrations'` and, for anything added, what reads it.

## 5. Caller sweep

Nothing can retire an identity code and say where its readers should go instead, so a writer given `MOVE` still accepts it as an identity.

**Expected output today:** no column for a successor need; both codes `active`; both needs present; every identity-bearing column holds 0 rows of either code (only the registry rows name them). If the output differs, the ground has moved: stop (section 9).

## 4. The change

Order of preference, from CLAUDE.md §8: do nothing and say why; change a rule or convention; reuse what exists; delete the cause; only then add the smallest code that closes the defect.

1. Schema migration: `base_taxonomy_identity.superseded_by_need TEXT REFERENCES access_needs(need_code)`, with a CHECK that it is set only when `status = 'deprecated'`. Create, copy, drop, rename; recreate every view and index that names the table (`select type, name from sqlite_master where sql like '%base_taxonomy_identity%'`). Never type the migration number: derive it (`ls scripts/migrations | grep -E '^[0-9]{3}_' | sort | tail -1`, plus one), and end it by setting `PRAGMA user_version` to it. Run `python3 scripts/audit/joined_cells_census.py` before and after; apply only with `python3 scripts/migrate_db.py`; prove with `python3 scripts/migrate_db.py --rebuild "$SCRATCH/rebuilt.db"` and `python3 scripts/audit/migration_reproducibility.py --deep`.
1a. **[Added 2026-11-12, OI-13 fold] The identity successor, in the same migration.** Also add `base_taxonomy_identity.superseded_by_identity TEXT REFERENCES base_taxonomy_identity(identity_code)`, and make the CHECK: a deprecated row has **exactly one** successor column set, an active row none (T-056 later adds a third successor column and widens this CHECK; it does not add a second mechanism). One mechanism serves both cases the owner's answers need: `SCI` retires to `WHEEL` (T-102) and `LMB` retires to `UPL` (T-116). A rename of the code was rejected: `identity_code` is a key other rows point at, and the 2026-09-16 ruling retires identifiers in place.
1b. **[Added 2026-11-12, OI-13 fold] Crossing-map rows retire in place.** `identity_icf_map` gains `retired_at`, `retired_by_session` and `retired_reason` (all NULL on a live row; a CHECK that the three are set together), and one verb `retire-population-icf-link --link-id N --reason "..." --session S`. Without it the refusal of item 2 is a dead end: `SCI` and `LMB` carry crossing rows (`select identity_code, count(*) from identity_icf_map where identity_code in ('SCI','LMB') group by 1`), and no verb removes or retires one. A crossing moves to a successor as a new row through the existing `add-population-icf-link` (its provenance names the old `link_id`) followed by retiring the old row; the table's `UNIQUE (identity_code, icf_code, mechanism)` already refuses a duplicate on the successor. A retired crossing is never un-retired. Every reader of `identity_icf_map` filters `retired_at IS NULL` first (the 2026-09-16 ruling's execution condition): find them with `git grep -n identity_icf_map -- scripts skills ':!scripts/migrations'` and `select name from sqlite_master where sql like '%identity_icf_map%'`.
2. One verb, `retire-identity --code (--need N | --to-identity C) --approval-ref H --reason R`, where `H` is the full text of a dated `## ` heading of `references/project-standards.md` found exactly once (corrected 2026-11-13 from a quoted ledger pointer: the one approval-pointer shape that T-024's `add-jurisdiction` and T-025's identity and pair verbs take for base admissions; T-025 section 4 names the check, `dbcore.require_approval_heading`; T-054 has no dependency on T-025, so it checks inline with `dbcore.ledger_heading_count`, as `add-jurisdiction` does today, and T-025's sweep converts that inline check to the helper when it merges. Chosen 2026-11-13, to avoid serialising T-054, T-056, T-114 and T-115 behind T-025), checked and printed in the result, not stored: sets `status = 'deprecated'` and `superseded_by_need`; never deletes. It refuses a code that any live row still carries (every column that takes an identity code, derived from the foreign keys into `base_taxonomy_identity`, not listed), naming the count and T-114's re-tag as the next action; and refuses a need that does not exist.

-- 135_identity_successor.sql
-- SCHEMA migration -- an identity code can be retired in place to the access need or the identity code that carries
-- it, and a crossing-map row can be retired in place. Tooling (workplan T-054, OD-37, OI-13 fold); no research rows.
--
-- WHY. MOVE and VES sit in the identity registry as populations, though the owner agreed they are access needs (OD-37),
-- and SCI and LMB are to be carried by WHEEL and UPL (T-102, T-116). Nothing could retire an identity code and say where
-- its readers should go, and nothing could retire a crossing row of identity_icf_map, so a retirement had no way to
-- finish. Identifiers are retired in place, never renamed or deleted (the 2026-09-16 ruling).
--
-- WHAT. base_taxonomy_identity gains superseded_by_need (an access_needs code) and superseded_by_identity (an identity
-- code). A DEPRECATED row names exactly ONE successor, an ACTIVE row none: one CHECK, carried by the second added
-- column (SQLite adds a column in place; a column CHECK may name the table's other columns, and it is tested on every
-- write of the row). identity_icf_map gains retired_at / retired_by_session / retired_reason, set together or not at all.
-- Every row stays; nothing is rewritten.
ALTER TABLE base_taxonomy_identity ADD COLUMN superseded_by_need TEXT REFERENCES access_needs(need_code);
ALTER TABLE base_taxonomy_identity ADD COLUMN superseded_by_identity TEXT REFERENCES base_taxonomy_identity(identity_code)
    CHECK ((status = 'deprecated' AND (superseded_by_need IS NOT NULL) + (superseded_by_identity IS NOT NULL) = 1)
        OR (status <> 'deprecated' AND superseded_by_need IS NULL AND superseded_by_identity IS NULL));

ALTER TABLE identity_icf_map ADD COLUMN retired_at TEXT;
ALTER TABLE identity_icf_map ADD COLUMN retired_by_session TEXT;
ALTER TABLE identity_icf_map ADD COLUMN retired_reason TEXT
    CHECK ((retired_at IS NULL AND retired_by_session IS NULL AND retired_reason IS NULL)
        OR (retired_at IS NOT NULL AND retired_by_session IS NOT NULL AND retired_reason IS NOT NULL));

EOF

| Task | T-055 |
| Title | Tooling for the mobility family: the devices it needs, and a parent's determination that gathers its children |
| Wave | 4 |
| Kind | **TOOLING** (CLAUDE.md rule 10: tooling and research never share a pull request) |
- **Tasks that must be merged to the integration base first:** T-019 merged (it carries T-018's link table, `v_live_lens_links`, and the engine's `_lens_clause`, which this task widens); and the design `T-102-design.md` present (it names the `device_class` values and the children; this task builds only what it names). Check by running that task's own after-test (its section 6), or `git log "$BASE" --oneline | grep -F "<that task's commit subject>"`.
- **Owner decisions that must be answered first.** The answer must be in `references/project-standards.md` (the ledger), in the owner's words.
- **Pilot or dry run** (a scratch clone, no pull request): do not run `/session-open`, do not touch `scratchpad/CURRENT`, stay on the branch you were given instead of `git switch -c`, and stop after section 7 (no push, no pull request, no `/batch-done`). Say in your report that it was a pilot.

## 3. The problem, in the guidebook's terms

The owner decomposed `MOB` by device. Wheelchair drive is already a typed descriptor (`device_class`), but the column cannot say "prosthesis", "crutches" or "cane", so a figure about those users would carry its device in prose or as an identity code (a second home, rule 5). And a determination at the parent `MOB` gathers only figures tagged `MOB`, so the family's commonality is lost.

**Evidence command** (read-only):

```
python3 -I -c "import sys,sqlite3;sys.path.insert(0,'scripts');import dbcore;c=sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro',uri=True);print(sorted(dbcore.check_values(c,'source_value_extractions','device_class')))"
grep -c parent_code scripts/assess/assess_cell.py
python3 -I -c "import sqlite3;c=sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro',uri=True);print(c.execute('select count(*) from base_taxonomy_identity where parent_code is not null').fetchone()[0])"
```

**Expected output today:** a list of the chair, walker, scooter, `mixed` and `not_device_scoped` values with none of `lower_limb_prosthesis`, `crutches`, `cane` (the vocabulary is read from the column's own CHECK, the way the writers read it); `0`; `0` (no code has a parent yet, which section 4 item 5 relies on). If the output differs, the ground has moved: stop (section 9).

Write it exactly in this form, beside `_lens_clause`:
   ```python
   # The identity lens is the one lens with a hierarchy (base_taxonomy_identity.parent_code): a cell keyed on a code
   # gathers the figures linked to that code or to any code whose parent_code chain reaches it (T-055). Derived from
   # the registry on every gather, never a list. UNION, not UNION ALL, so a cycle ends.
   _IDENTITY_FAMILY = ("(WITH RECURSIVE family AS (SELECT ? AS code UNION SELECT i.identity_code "
                       "FROM base_taxonomy_identity i JOIN family f ON i.parent_code = f.code) "
                       "SELECT code FROM family)")
   ```
   and in `_lens_clause`, for `c == "identity_code"`, put `k.identity_code IN {_IDENTITY_FAMILY}` where the other lenses keep `k.{c} = ?` (the one parameter is still `lens[c]`). Two things about this form are required, not style:
   - **No column list on the CTE.** `T-018-design.md` section 4 sketches `WITH RECURSIVE family(code) AS (…)`. The blocking `schema_reference_audit` recognises a CTE name only by `WITH [RECURSIVE] <name> AS` (`grep -n 'RECURSIVE' scripts/audit/schema_reference_audit.py`), so with a column list it reads `family` as a table the schema lacks: `MISSING: family`, `RESULT: FAIL` (pilot, 2026-11-13). The form above names the column inside (`SELECT ? AS code`) and passes.
   - **A parenthesised subquery inside the `IN`, not a top-level `WITH`.** The engine splices `_lens_clause`'s text into the `WHERE` of five different `SELECT`s, so there is no statement head to put a `WITH` on.
   **A figure is gathered once** [2026-11-12, OI-13 fold]: the children are not mutually exclusive (a figure may carry `WHEEL` and `WALKAID` links), so the family predicate stays inside the per-figure `EXISTS`, never a join on the links, and no count downstream (governing figures, sources, convergence roots) multiplies by the number of links. Update the docstring of `_lens_clause` to say so. In `gather_extraction_links`, the `excluded` reason becomes "… carries every code the cell states (an identity code counts through its `parent_code` chain); …": keep its prefix `not stated in this cell's lens (` exactly, because T-019's cases match it. (`SCI` is retired to `WHEEL` and `LMB` becomes `UPL`, outside the family, by T-102 and T-116; neither changes this task. The ninth set replaced the child `PROSTH` by `LLD`, people with lower-limb differences, defined by the condition: `lower_limb_prosthesis` stays a `device_class` value, a descriptor of the device a figure concerns, and is still added here; it is not a second home of `LLD`, `T-102-design.md` §0. _Q = ("SELECT DISTINCT x.extraction_id FROM source_value_extractions x JOIN v_live_lens_links l "
          "USING (extraction_id) WHERE x.parameter_id = ? AND l.identity_code = ?")
    _pairs = _live.execute("SELECT DISTINCT x.parameter_id, l.identity_code FROM v_live_lens_links l "
                           "JOIN source_value_extractions x USING (extraction_id) "
                           "WHERE l.identity_code IS NOT NULL ORDER BY 1, 2").fetchall() if _live else []
    if not _pairs:
        print("      SKIPPED-NO-FIXTURE: T019-13..15 need the live database with identity links on figures")
    else:
        _bad, _reached = [], 0
        for pid, code in _pairs:
            d = determine(_live, pid, _mob(code), "syn-slug", "t019-live")
            inl = {l["extraction_id"] for l in d["links"] if l["in_lens"]}
            _reached += len(inl)
            carries = {r[0] for r in _live.execute(_Q, (pid, code))}
            out_ok = all(l["role"] == "excluded" and (l["exclusion_reason"] or "").startswith(LENS_REASON)
                         for l in d["links"] if not l["in_lens"])
            gov_ok = all(l["extraction_id"] in carries for l in d["links"] if l["role"] != "excluded")
            if not (inl and inl == carries and out_ok and gov_ok):
                _bad.append((pid, code))
        expect("T019-13 (AT-50): for every (parameter, identity code) the live links name, the figures "
               f"a cell reaches are exactly those carrying its code ({len(_pairs)} cells, {_reached} "
               "figures reached), none is empty, and every other figure of the parameter is linked "
               "`excluded` with the lens reason", not _bad and _reached > 0, str(_bad))

        # AT-51 live: every parameter whose figures carry ALL and another identity, cell by cell. The
        # equality (reached == carrying) holds for each; whether a cell has a NON-EXCLUDED row is derived,
        # and the case says so when no ALL cell has one, since then nothing plays a part there.
        _ap = _live.execute("SELECT DISTINCT x.parameter_id, o.identity_code FROM source_value_extractions x "
                            "JOIN v_live_lens_links a ON a.extraction_id = x.extraction_id "
                            "AND a.identity_code = 'ALL' JOIN source_value_extractions y "
                            "ON y.parameter_id = x.parameter_id JOIN v_live_lens_links o "
                            "ON o.extraction_id = y.extraction_id AND o.identity_code <> 'ALL' "
                            "ORDER BY 1, 2").fetchall()
        if not _ap:
            print("      SKIPPED-NO-FIXTURE: T019-14 needs a parameter whose figures carry ALL and "
                  "another identity")
        else:
            ok, _played = True, 0
            for pid, other in _ap:
                for code in ("ALL", other):
                    d = determine(_live, pid, _mob(code), "syn-slug", "t019-live")
                    inl = {l["extraction_id"] for l in d["links"] if l["in_lens"]}
                    ok &= inl == {r[0] for r in _live.execute(_Q, (pid, code))} and bool(inl)
                    ok &= all(_live.execute("SELECT 1 FROM v_live_lens_links WHERE extraction_id = ? "
                                            "AND identity_code = ?", (l["extraction_id"], code)).fetchone()
                              for l in d["links"] if l["role"] != "excluded")
                    _played += code == "ALL" and any(l["role"] != "excluded" for l in d["links"])
            expect("T019-14 (AT-51, live): every ALL cell reaches exactly the figures carrying ALL, and every "
                   "other identity's cell reaches an ALL-tagged figure only if it also carries that identity "
                   f"({_played} of the ALL cells hold a non-excluded row)",
                   ok, f"{len(_ap)} parameter/identity pairs")
